paras: The lynching of Jim Devine was the hanging of a man known as Jim Devine, alias Jones, by a party of men at Raton City, New Mexico Territory, in mid-April 1881, after he was accused of assaulting two men there. Telegraph reports from Denver placed the lynching "near Las Vegas" on Saturday night, April 16, and described Devine as an escaped California convict with a reward on his head. The story ran as a brief in papers from California to Kentucky, usually beside other Western killings.

According to the Las Vegas Morning Gazette, Devine had worked for nearly two months as a freight brakeman on the railroad division between Raton and Las Vegas. The paper said he was discharged a week or more before the lynching after an elderly passenger complained to Trainmaster Saunders that Devine had robbed him on the run to Raton. Devine then stayed around Raton with a companion named Bowman, and the Gazette accused the pair of carrying passengers in box cars for cash and of drinking and gambling.

On Friday, the Gazette reported, Devine and Bowman beat the elderly man who had complained, and then clubbed and knifed a man named "Gartiug," whom the paper called "a quiet, peaceable fellow" and described as lying in critical condition. Bowman escaped, but Devine was caught and locked in a store room "for safe kecpiirg [keeping], pending trial." At 11 o'clock that night a party of men took him from the store room to a piñón tree and hanged him with a bell rope.

Passengers on the southbound train passing Raton City on Sunday forenoon saw the body hanging from the tree, not far from the hotel and the track. After the hanging, the Gazette said, it was learned that Devine had escaped from San Quentin penitentiary in California, where a standing reward of $1,200 had been offered for his arrest.
No report of an inquest, of any arrest of the men who hanged Devine, or of what became of Bowman or the wounded man appears in the coverage.

The Gazette's account, headed "JONES JERKED" with the subhead "To m Speedy Judgment and Eternity," called Devine "a victim of Judge Lynch" and dwelt on his character, describing him as "old in sin and iniquity." It did not criticize the men who hanged him.

Outside New Mexico the story traveled as a one-sentence special from the Denver Tribune, dated April 18, which the Sacramento Daily Record-Union, the Chicago Daily Tribune and the Salt Lake Herald printed on April 19. The Chicago paper ran it under "WESTERN MURDERS" beside a Deming restaurant keeper's killing of a Chinese man, and the Sacramento paper headlined it "An Escaped Convict from California Lynched in New Mexico." Over the next ten days the item appeared in weekly news columns in Ohio, Kentucky, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Iowa, often next to the lynching of an elderly Black woman in Laurens County, South Carolina. None of the reports gave Devine's race.

The wire versions said Devine was lynched for an "attempt to murder a section hand," while the Lexington Weekly Intelligencer shortened this to "the murder of a section hand." A Memphis Daily Appeal version named the section hand as Campbell, a name that appears in the same Denver dispatch for the Deming restaurant keeper. The local Gazette instead described assaults on an elderly man and on "Gartiug," without calling either a section hand.

The wires dated the lynching to Saturday night and placed it near Las Vegas, but the Mower County Transcript said "the 17th." The Gazette, the only paper from the territory, put the hanging at Raton City on the night of Devine's arrest after Friday's assaults, with the body seen Sunday morning. The reward was given as $1,400 in the wire reports and $1,200 in the Gazette.

bases: A party of men took Devine from a store room where he was held pending trial and hanged him from a piñón tree (A1); wire reports called it a lynching (A2, A5).

A 'party of men' took Devine from custody pending trial and hanged him as 'a victim of Judge Lynch' after he was accused of beating and knifing two men (A1); the wires report he was 'lynched' for attempted murder (A2, A5). The party's size is not given, but a 'party of men' implies several.

The local Las Vegas Gazette account (A1) and the independent Denver Tribune wire (A2, A5) agree that Devine alias Jones was lynched in New Mexico on the weekend of April 16-17, though they differ on place, charge and reward.
